## Q5
Dialog control is a function of which layer?

## Q5 - Options
(A) Network Layer
(B) Transport Layer
(C) Session Layer
(D) Presentation Layer

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q38

Dialog control refers to managing whose turn it is to transmit in a conversation between two communicating systems, deciding whether communication is half-duplex or full-duplex.

The session layer of the OSI model is responsible for establishing, managing, and terminating sessions between applications, and dialog control is one of its core functions.

- **A. Network Layer** — handles routing and logical addressing, not turn-taking between applications.
- **B. Transport Layer** — handles end-to-end delivery and reliability, not who transmits next.
- **C. Session Layer** — correct. It manages dialog control between communicating applications.
- **D. Presentation Layer** — handles data translation, encryption, and compression, not dialog turn-taking.

## Q6
Match List-I (Network protocols) with List-II (OSI/TCP-IP layers).

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. SMTP | I. Application layer |
| B. BGP | II. Transport layer |
| C. TCP | III. Data Link Layer |
| D. PPP | IV. Network Layer |

## Q6 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
(C) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
(D) A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q85

SMTP operates at the Application layer since it defines how mail clients and servers exchange messages, so A pairs with I.<br>
TCP is a core Transport-layer protocol responsible for reliable end-to-end delivery, so C pairs with II.<br>
PPP is a Data Link-layer protocol used to establish point-to-point serial connections, so D pairs with III.<br>
BGP is the protocol routers use to exchange reachability information between autonomous systems, and it is classified here as the remaining Network-layer routing protocol, so B pairs with IV.

A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III is the only option that correctly places SMTP at Application, TCP at Transport, and PPP at Data Link, making it the internally consistent match.

## Q8
Match List I with List II on OSI network layers.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Physical layer | I. Transforming the raw bits in the form of frame for transmission |
| B. Data Link Layer | II. Control and monitoring of subnet |
| C. Network layer | III. Transmission of raw bits over communication channel |
| D. Transport layer | IV. Datagrams transmission data through connection oriented or connectionless using datagram |

List I / List II: OSI layer functions

## Q8 - Options
(A) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
(C) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
(D) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q70

Each OSI layer matches its defining function.

- The physical layer is responsible for the raw transmission of bits over the communication channel — A-III.
- The data link layer packages those raw bits into frames for reliable transmission across one link — B-I.
- The network layer is responsible for controlling and monitoring the subnet, primarily through routing — C-II.
- The transport layer delivers data end-to-end as datagrams, using either connection-oriented or connectionless service — D-IV.

This gives the mapping A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

- **A. A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV** — swaps the data link and network layer pairings.
- **B. A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV** — misassigns the physical, data link, and network layer pairings.
- **C. A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV** — correct, matches every pairing above.
- **D. A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III** — misassigns three of the four pairings.

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q73

Each OSI layer is matched to the function it is specifically responsible for.

The Physical Layer is concerned with transmitting raw, unstructured bits over the physical communication channel, giving A-III.

The Data Link Layer takes those raw bits and organizes them into structured frames for reliable transmission over a single link, giving B-I.

The Network Layer is responsible for routing and for the overall control and monitoring of the subnet as packets move between networks, giving C-II.

The Transport Layer delivers data end to end using either connection-oriented service (like TCP) or connectionless service (like UDP), giving D-IV.

This gives the mapping A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

## Q11
Which layer divides each message into packets at the source and re-assembles them at the destination?

## Q11 - Options
(A) Network layer
(B) Transport layer
(C) Data link layer
(D) Physical layer

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q39

The network layer is responsible for routing individual packets end to end, and in the classic layer-function description it is the layer that divides an outgoing message into packets at the source and reassembles the incoming packets back into the original message at the destination. The data link layer instead frames and error-checks data over one physical hop, and the physical layer only converts bits into electrical or optical signals.

## Q15
In the TCP/IP model, encryption and decryption are functions of \_\_\_\_\_\_ layer.

## Q15 - Options
(A) data link
(B) network
(C) transport
(D) application

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q10

In the standard TCP/IP protocol suite, the Application layer absorbs the responsibilities of the OSI Session and Presentation layers.

Data encryption, decryption, compression, and format conversions are handled either directly within application protocols or through security sublayers like TLS and SSL operating at the application level.

## Q16
Which of the following statements is/are true with regard to various layers in the Internet stack?<br>
P: At the link layer, a packet of transmitted information is called a frame.<br>
Q: At the network layer, a packet of transmitted information is called a segment.

## Q16 - Options
(A) P only
(B) Q only
(C) P and Q
(D) Neither P nor Q

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q70

Packet data units are named according to their architectural layer:

- **P** is true because data link layer packets encapsulated with MAC headers and trailers are called frames.
- **Q** is false because packets at the network layer are called datagrams (or IP packets). Segments are protocol data units formed at the transport layer (e.g. TCP segments).

Only statement P is true.

## Q17
Consider ISO-OSI network architecture reference model. Session layer of this model offers dialog control, token management and \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ as services.

## Q17 - Options
(A) Flow Control
(B) Syncronization
(C) Errors
(D) Asyncronization

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OSI Model & Layer Responsibilities
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q36

In the OSI reference model, the primary services provided by the Session layer are dialog control, token management, and synchronization.

- Synchronization allows the session layer to insert checkpoints into long data streams so that only data transmitted after the most recent checkpoint is retransmitted following a network crash.
- Dialog control regulates communication turns in half-duplex or full-duplex transmission.
- Token management prevents conflicting attempts to execute critical operations simultaneously.
- Flow control (Option A) and error control (Option C) are managed by the data link and transport layers.
- Therefore, Option B is correct.
